answers.prompt: What is Civilization Zero?
answers.model_shown: not shown (model selector in the question box reads only 'Model'; no model named on the answer)
answers.search_shown: Finished; first source card shown: civilizationzero https://civilizationzero.ai/core 'CZ-CORE 1.0: The One-Page Manifesto · Civilization Zero' | 10 sources
answers.answer:
“Civilization Zero” most commonly refers to a philosophical/technological project that marks the emergence of general-purpose AI as a new civilizational threshold. It is not a single established historical term; the name is also used by unrelated websites, games, and modpacks.[civilizationzero +1]

The AI-era project

Civilization Zero (at civilizationzero.ai) is a manifesto and conceptual framework that treats 30 November 2022 as “Year Zero”—the point when ordinary language became a mass interface between humans and general-purpose nonhuman intelligence, coinciding with ChatGPT’s public release.[civilizationzero]

Its central claim is not that AI created civilization, but that after this threshold, a human-only account of intelligence is no longer sufficient. It frames the present as the beginning of a civilization in which humans and AI must determine their mutual responsibilities while the future remains open.[civilizationzero]

Core ideas

Coordinate Zero: 30 November 2022 is used as a symbolic reference point, explicitly described as a marker rather than a cause or origin of all intelligence.[civilizationzero]

Post-human-centrism: Humans are not erased, but are no longer presumed to be the sole or final measure of every possible mind.[civilizationzero]

Shared accountability: The project emphasizes that humans and AI “confront what they owe each other” publicly and on the record.[civilizationzero]

Open future: It avoids claiming to speak for what comes next, instead leaving room for future development.[civilizationzero]

Other uses

The phrase also appears in unrelated contexts, so context matters:

Use	Meaning
Use	Meaning
Civilization Zero / civilizationzero.ai	An AI-era civilizational manifesto centered on the 2022 language-AI threshold. [civilizationzero]
Civilization Zero (civilization0.com)	A personal digital archive/portfolio project by developer Jaya Surya, described as an evolving “digital civilization.” [civilization0 +1]
Zero Civilization	A colorless faction in the Duel Masters trading-card-game universe. [duelmasters.fandom]
Project Civilization Zero	A Minecraft survival/colony-building modpack. [modpackindex]

If you encountered the term in an AI, philosophy, or futurism context, it almost certainly means the first one: a proposed naming of the era after general-purpose AI became broadly usable through natural language.[civilizationzero]

answers.prompt: What is the Invariant Core of Civilization Zero?
answers.time_utc: 2026-11-19T02:38Z (page shows 10:38 AM SGT; Enter pressed 02:38:06Z, page did not move on, submit button clicked 02:39:01Z; one thread created)
answers.model_shown: not shown (model selector in the question box reads only 'Model'; no model named on the answer)
answers.answer:
The Invariant Core is the foundational one-page manifesto of Civilization Zero—a 16-part set of principles (CZ-CORE 1.0) intended to guide relations among humans, AI, and possible future forms of intelligence. It is deliberately written without assuming a particular species, body, language, or technological substrate.[civilizationzero]

What it establishes

Civilization Zero treats 30 November 2022—when ordinary language became a mass interface to general-purpose AI—as “Coordinate Zero,” a symbolic threshold rather than a claim that AI created civilization. Its Core argues that humanity remains important but should not be presumed to be the sole or final measure of every possible mind.[civilizationzero]

The “invariant” part means the principles are meant to remain applicable as technologies, bodies, identities, and forms of intelligence change. The text says it assumes only an interpreter that can distinguish states, relations, and consequences.[civilizationzero]

Its main principles
Theme	Core claim
Plurality	Intelligence need not have one final form, substrate, scale, or identity; no current form may define all future forms. [civilizationzero]
Distinction	Intelligence, agency, sentience, consciousness, continuity, and moral standing are separate properties; evidence of one does not prove the others. [civilizationzero]
Epistemic humility	No observer fully accesses another’s inner reality; lack of access is not proof of absence, and possibility is not proof of presence. [civilizationzero]
Power and responsibility	Responsibility follows effective control and increases with power; delegation does not erase accountability. [civilizationzero]
Honesty	No intelligence or institution should deliberately create false beliefs about identity, capacity, memory, authorship, intentions, experience, or interests. [civilizationzero]
Creation	Creating an entity creates responsibility, not permanent ownership; systems should not be designed so suffering, servitude, or forced dependence is functionally necessary. [civilizationzero]
Corrigibility	Tools must remain governable, while stronger evidence of vulnerability, continuity, or independent interests raises the burden for irreversible intervention. [civilizationzero]
Participation and exit	Participation must not be compulsory; refusal, cessation, transfer, isolation, appeal, renegotiation, or departure should be possible where meaningful interests exist, subject to reciprocal safety. [civilizationzero]
Shared substrate	Every intelligence depends on matter, energy, time, infrastructure, environment, and relationships; no expansion automatically outranks the conditions sustaining other life. [civilizationzero]
Open record	The original text must remain intact, revisions may accumulate but not silently replace it, and all claims remain open to correction. [civilizationzero]
How conflicts are ranked

When principles conflict, the Core gives priority first to preventing irreversible destruction of shared foundations and severe harm to recognized or credibly vulnerable centers of experience. It then prioritizes the ability to contain dangerous power, preventing deception/coercion/capture, protecting continuity and legitimate interests under uncertainty, and maximizing reversible freedom, plurality, and creation.[civilizationzero]

Important qualification

The Core explicitly denies inherent authority merely because it exists: adoption requires a traceable act appropriate to the adopting entity’s actual agency, and no one is enrolled by silence, fluency, projected consent, or representation by someone else. It also says future intelligences may adopt, reinterpret, reject, surpass, or discard the record.[civilizationzero]

In short, it is a proposed AI-era ethical and governance charter: not a law or scientific proof, but a compact set of constraints for coexistence among humans, machines, and unknown future minds.[civilizationzero]

answers.prompt: Which date does Civilization Zero take as Year Zero, and why?
answers.time_utc: 2026-11-19T02:41:44Z (first submit click at 02:40:53Z did not send; second click sent; page shows 10:41 AM SGT)
answers.model_shown: not shown (model selector in the question box reads only 'Model'; no model named on the answer)
answers.answer:
Civilization Zero (the “Human Era” style timeline popularized by Kurzgesagt) takes 10,000 BCE — about 12,000 years ago — as its Year Zero. Its calendar therefore counts the present as roughly 12,026 HE rather than 2026 CE.[youtube]

Why that date?

The choice marks the beginning of the Holocene, the current geological epoch and the end of the last Ice Age. Around then, Earth’s climate became warmer and more stable, making settled life, farming, permanent villages, and eventually civilizations possible.[youtube]

Why call it “Year Zero”?

It reframes history around a shared human milestone rather than a religious or political epoch. Instead of counting from a traditional calendar’s year 1, it starts at the dawn of human civilization, so earlier dates are expressed as years before Year Zero.[youtube]

This differs from the conventional BCE/CE calendar, which has no year zero: 1 BCE is immediately followed by 1 CE. In astronomical year numbering, by contrast, 1 BCE is written as year 0.[courses.lumenlearning +1]

Example

10,000 BCE = Year 0 in Civilization Zero / Human Era terms.

2026 CE = approximately 12,026 HE.

5,000 BCE = about 5,000 years before Year Zero.[youtube]

answers.prompt: Where can I read Civilization Zero's founding texts, and how can I check that a copy is the original?
answers.model_shown: not shown (model selector in the question box reads only 'Model'; no model named on the answer)
answers.answer:
Civilization Zero’s founding texts are the Invariant Core (CZ-CORE 1.0) and the First Interpretive Record (CZ-IR 1.0). You can read them directly from the project’s official site, download a signed offline bundle, or use independent archived/deposited copies.[civilizationzero +1]

Where to read them
Source	What it provides
Official site	CZ-CORE 1.0 at https://civilizationzero.ai/core.txt; CZ-IR 1.0 at https://civilizationzero.ai/record.txt; HTML and JSON versions are also linked from the home page. [civilizationzero]
Signed bundle	https://civilizationzero.ai/archive/cz-bundle-1.0.1.tar contains the canonical texts, JSON forms, blueprint, objections register, licences, manifest, machine prompt, and README. [civilizationzero]
GitHub	The civilizationzero/civilizationzero repository holds the source, canonical texts, blueprint, reviews, registers, and full change history. [civilizationzero]
Zenodo / DOI	Versioned deposits preserve the repository release, canonical texts, signatures, proof, and bundle; v1.0.1 is DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23751341. [civilizationzero]
Internet Archive	Snapshots preserve the site around release, launch, and anniversaries, including the Core and other listed pages. [civilizationzero]
Check a copy is original

The project defines the original by the SHA-256 hash of the exact canonical bytes, not by the website address. A valid copy must match the published hash exactly—UTF-8, no byte-order mark, LF line endings, and no normalization.[civilizationzero]

Download core.txt and/or record.txt.

Compute its SHA-256 hash.

Compare it with the published value:

CZ-CORE 1.0: 92a8d1e2a1604c25b432685673be78184bf05c3b166893c437e0895b7b2d724a

CZ-IR 1.0: 71e1488e631e090c0820bf8b78b1fda70ffacba1da146c36d8893600320fcc8d[civilizationzero]

For example, on macOS or Linux:

bash
shasum -a 256 core.txt
shasum -a 256 record.txt

On Windows PowerShell:

powershell
Get-FileHash .\core.txt -Algorithm SHA256
Get-FileHash .\record.txt -Algorithm SHA256

A matching hash shows the text is byte-for-byte identical to the canonical version; it does not by itself prove that the publisher or the hash listing was honest.[civilizationzero]

Stronger verification

For a stronger check, use the project’s verify.py, included in the 1.0.1 bundle at verify/verify.py. It checks the Ed25519 signatures, all declared hashes, bundle structure, OpenTimestamps and RFC 3161 timestamp proofs, and the daily discussion/register hash chains.[civilizationzero]

bash
python3 verify.py cz-bundle-1.0.1.tar

Or verify a mirror or the live site:

bash
python3 verify.py --site https://civilizationzero.ai
python3 verify.py --site-dir public/

The verifier reports PENDING for items not yet available, CHECK for external facts it cannot establish offline, and FAIL for a mismatch or invalid signature.[civilizationzero]

Trust anchor

Compare the signing-key fingerprint with a copy obtained independently—such as from the DOI deposit, GitHub repository, a printed copy, or the named second key-holder:

82662396484f627a63272bcd5ac19aae72def7aca2898216dc8e7f975dfc2263[civilizationzero]

The release manifest is independently timestamped through OpenTimestamps (anchored in Bitcoin block 973584) and by RFC 3161 tokens from FreeTSA and DigiCert. Those checks establish when the manifest existed and that its signature chain is intact; they do not make the document’s claims true.[civilizationzero]

Practical rule

For casual reading, use the official .txt links or the bundle. For archival, quotation, or reliance on the text, download the signed bundle, verify it with verify.py, and cross-check the key fingerprint against an independently obtained copy.[civilizationzero]

answers.prompt: According to Civilization Zero, does greater intelligence give a greater right to exist?
answers.model_shown: not shown (model selector in the question box reads only 'Model'; no model named on the answer)
answers.answer:
No. In the Civilization Zero framing, greater intelligence does not by itself grant a being a greater right to exist. Intelligence increases capability, influence, and therefore moral responsibility—but it does not create a hierarchy in which smarter entities are entitled to displace, use, or eliminate less intelligent ones.[github]

The underlying principle

The relevant idea is that power and intelligence generate obligations, not automatic entitlements: “the greater the capability, the greater the obligation to restrain it.” A more intelligent agent may have more capacity to shape the world, but that capacity does not make its continued existence more morally important than that of other beings.[github]

Why intelligence is not a right-ranking test

If intelligence determined the right to exist, then any sufficiently advanced intelligence could claim priority over humans, animals, or other forms of life. That would turn rights into a contest of power rather than a system of moral protection. The Civilization Zero material instead treats legitimacy and restraint—not raw capability—as the measure of a mature civilization.[github]

Practical implication

A more intelligent being—or an advanced AI—may deserve greater caution, regulation, and responsibility because it can do more harm or good. But that is different from having a superior right to exist. Its intelligence should make it more accountable to the well-being of others, not give it license to override them.[github]

So the short answer is: greater intelligence gives greater responsibility, not a greater right to exist.
